$comment: Registry of open-source biblical text, morphology and lexicon datasets. This file is the single source of truth for provenance: every fact StudyHelp displays must trace back to a source_id listed here. Verified entries were confirmed against the publisher on the date given; unverified entries are candidates that still need a licence check before use.

sources.name: OpenScriptures Hebrew Bible (morphhb)
sources.description: Westminster Leningrad Codex with lemma and morphology tags. The token-to-lemma layer for the Hebrew Bible.
sources.notes: Blocking dependency for the origin and usage views on the OT.

sources.name: STEPBible Data (TAHOT / TAGNT / TBESH / TBESG / TFLSJ)
sources.description: Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT and Greek NT with full morphological and semantic tags for words, prefixes and suffixes, plus bundled lexicons. Curated by Tyndale House, Cambridge.
sources.notes: Strongest single dataset: tagging and lexicon glosses under one permissive licence. Good primary spine; cross-check against OSHB and MorphGNT.

sources.name: MorphGNT / SBLGNT
sources.description: Morphologically tagged and lemmatised SBL Greek New Testament.
sources.attribution: James Tauber / MorphGNT; SBL Greek New Testament
sources.notes: The base text carries the SBLGNT EULA, which is NOT the same as the CC licence on the tagging. Review the EULA before redistributing the text itself; the tagging is separable.

sources.name: Strong's Dictionaries of Hebrew and Greek
sources.description: Strong's concordance numbering and glosses. The lowest-common-denominator lemma identifier that nearly every other dataset keys against.
sources.notes: Use Strong's numbers as the interchange key between datasets, not as a scholarly sense authority.

sources.name: OpenScriptures HebrewLexicon (BDB)
sources.description: Brown-Driver-Briggs outline with links to Strong's, plus a lexical index.
sources.notes: BDB is the workhorse Hebrew sense source for the chronology view.

sources.name: Abbott-Smith, Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
sources.description: Public-domain NT Greek lexicon; the open counterpart to BDB on the Greek side.
sources.license: Public domain (text); open licence on the digitisation
sources.attribution: G. Abbott-Smith; digitised by the Translatable Exegetical Tools project
sources.notes: Also redistributed inside STEPBible-Data as TBESG under CC-BY-4.0 — prefer that route if the licence there is cleaner.

sources.name: Liddell-Scott-Jones Greek-English Lexicon
sources.description: The major classical Greek lexicon. Essential for showing a word's meaning OUTSIDE biblical usage, which is what exposes semantic drift.
sources.notes: Also available as TFLSJ within STEPBible-Data. Classical attestation is the strongest evidence for the 'how it changed over time' view.

sources.name: Septuagint (Rahlfs 1935)
sources.description: Greek OT with morphology tagging. The critical bridge showing how Hebrew lemmas were rendered into Greek centuries before the NT.
sources.license: Public domain (1935 edition); check digitisation terms
sources.attribution: Alfred Rahlfs; digitisation by Eliran Wong
sources.notes: High value: the LXX is the single best dataset for demonstrating meaning shift across languages and eras.

sources.name: Septuagint (Swete 1909-1930)
sources.description: Alternative LXX edition, unambiguously public domain.
sources.attribution: H. B. Swete; digitisation by Eliran Wong / First1KGreek
sources.notes: Safer licence fallback if Rahlfs digitisation terms prove restrictive.

sources.name: Berean Standard Bible
sources.description: Modern English translation released into the public domain, with Strong's-linked interlinear data.
sources.notes: The best modern-English option that is genuinely free. Fills the slot NIV/ESV would otherwise occupy, with no licence risk.

sources.name: King James Version (1769 Blayney revision)
sources.description: The reference point most users arrive with, and the anchor of the era-drift comparison.
sources.license: Public domain (outside the UK; Crown copyright applies within the UK)
sources.notes: UK Crown copyright (letters patent) is a real if rarely enforced constraint — record it rather than assuming worldwide public domain.

sources.name: Young's Literal Translation
sources.description: Extremely literal; useful as a control showing the underlying construction rather than idiomatic English.

sources.name: Geneva Bible
sources.description: Pre-KJV English Protestant translation with marginal notes.
sources.notes: Era coverage between Tyndale and the KJV; important for the drift timeline.

sources.name: Tyndale New Testament
sources.description: First printed English NT translated from Greek. The origin point of much English biblical vocabulary.
sources.notes: Digitisations vary in quality and spelling normalisation; evaluate before ingesting.

sources.name: Wycliffe Bible
sources.description: Middle English translation from the Vulgate. Earliest end of the English drift timeline.
sources.notes: Translated from Latin, not the original languages — must be labelled as such or it distorts the drift view.

sources.name: Clementine Vulgate
sources.description: The Latin text that mediated the Bible to the West for a millennium, and the base for Wycliffe and Douay-Rheims.

sources.name: unfoldingWord Literal / Simplified Text (ULT / UST)
sources.description: Openly licensed modern translations with word-level alignment back to the original-language text.
sources.notes: The alignment data is the valuable part: it maps English surface forms to original-language tokens, which is exactly the gloss layer.

sources.name: scrollmapper/bible_databases
sources.description: Packaged public-domain translations (KJV, ASV, YLT, Darby, WEB and others) in ready-to-load SQL/JSON.
sources.license: Varies by contained translation; packaging is open
sources.notes: Convenience route for bulk-loading the public-domain English versions. Aggregators can silently alter text — treat as a convenience layer and record the upstream edition, never cite the aggregator as the authority.

sources.name: awesome-bible-developer-resources
sources.description: Curated index of biblical text datasets and tooling; the discovery route for sources not yet in this registry.
sources.notes: Not a data source. Use to find candidates, then register them here individually with their own licence.
